rationale: The study examines Filipino public opinion, national security concerns and presidential approval ratings in relation to the US-led war in Iraq. It does not address household or community water or sanitation service access (fails Criterion 1 and Criterion 4; Exclusion Code E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both readings as an off-topic political science and public opinion study on foreign policy and presidential ratings during the Iraq War, with no connection to water or sanitation services.

evidence_quotes.quote: Filipino Public Opinion, Presidential Leadership and the US-Led War in Iraq
The majority of Filipinos wanted the government to take a neutral stance in the fight against Iraq.
With the quick end to the war, public anxiety declined, government efforts to keep the country secure and stable were recognized and the President's ratings improved.
